rationale: Comprehensive phenotypic profiling of the defining cohort of 45 individuals with bi-allelic pathogenic ACBD6 variants confirms that microcephaly is an inconsistent manifestation, presenting in only 39% of patients overall (and congenital microcephaly in 33%, 7/21). Consequently, normal head circumference is present in the majority (>60%) of affected individuals and does not exclude ACBD6-related neurodevelopmental disorder.

evidence.text: In an international cohort of 45 affected individuals harboring bi-allelic ACBD6 mutations, microcephaly was documented in only 39% of patients, whereas features like global developmental delay (100%), movement disorders (97%), facial dysmorphism (95%), and even overweight status (59%) were substantially more frequent.

source.title: Bi-allelic ACBD6 variants lead to a neurodevelopmental syndrome with progressive and complex movement disorders
source.quote: The affected individuals (23 males and 22 females), aged 1-50 years, typically present with a complex and progressive disease involving moderate-to-severe global developmental delay/intellectual disability (100%) with significant expressive language impairment (98%), movement disorders (97%), facial dysmorphism (95%) and mild cerebellar ataxia (85%) associated with gait impairment (94%), limb spasticity/hypertonia (76%), oculomotor (71%) and behavioural abnormalities (65%), overweight (59%), microcephaly (39%) and epilepsy (33%).

evidence.text: Detailed measurements across the cohort demonstrate that head circumference at birth was at or below the 3rd percentile in only 7 of 21 assessed patients (33%), confirming that congenital microcephaly is also present in only a minority of cases.

new_directions.question_text: Does the presence or absence of microcephaly in ACBD6 deficiency correlate with specific variant classes (e.g., complete loss-of-function versus hypomorphic missense variants) or brain malformation patterns?
new_directions.rationale: Determining genotype-phenotype correlations could explain why approximately 39% develop microcephaly while the remainder remain normocephalic.

new_directions.question_text: Is microcephaly in ACBD6 deficiency progressive postnatally, and what are the longitudinal head circumference trajectory z-scores across childhood?
new_directions.rationale: Birth head circumference was <= 3rd percentile in 33% (7/21) while overall microcephaly was 39%, suggesting deceleration of head growth might occur in a subset of normocephalic neonates.
